kurz: Cheese is curdled milk protein with fat. Whether it melts creamily or turns stringy and greasy depends on age, moisture and acidity.
bild_im_kopf: Like a net of protein with fat and water trapped inside.
was_passiert: When melting, the protein network loosens. Young, moist cheeses melt creamily. Very old, dry cheeses tend to release fat. Too much heat makes the protein contract: rubbery, with pools of fat.
faustregeln: Grate finely and melt over medium heat.
For fondue, white wine and a little starch: acid and starch hold the [[emulsion|emulsion]] together.
Stir parmesan into pasta only over medium heat.
